fixed.item: Found while measuring the fabric system: with the kernel's rain law deferred (the current state) a dry textile left out in the rain never got wet -- _tick_textile's rain rule only reached textiles the fabric system already processed (wet ones, ones set out with hang_dry), so a dry shirt on the lawn stayed at wetness 0.0 through 30 min of rain while a slightly damp one was soaked to 0.95
fixed.how: house_sim/systems/textiles_laundry/dry.py: rain_rooms(w) (uncovered outdoor rooms while the weather condition is rain and physical.kernel_rain is false), _in_the_rain (the kernel's exposure rule, the exposure modes of _tick_textile, not another domain's dried records) and _needs_tick(..., rain): a textile out in the weather in such a room needs a tick, so the existing rule soaks it. The idle probes and idle notes of both fabric systems treat a textile in a rain room like an active heater (textiles_in_rain), so they stay exact; the wrinkle run skips those textiles as it skips other ticking ones. With the rain law active the kernel wets things and this rule stands down. Probes on vs off in 14 rainy generated houses (gen 2 seeds 0-11, gen 1 seeds 0-1, 2 h): identical states; the one exposed front-yard coir doormat (gen 2 seed 1) is soaked, the porch ones stay dry (scratch rain_probe_exact.py).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_dry_laundry_left_out_in_the_rain_is_soaked_and_sheltered_laundry_stays_dry (lawn shirt soaked and rained_on; one in a closed bin and one indoors stay dry; probes on/off identical; rain law forced with a rain rate: rain_rooms empty, the kernel wets it). Fails on HEAD's code.

fixed.item: P1 gate G7 (substep cost): the fabric system evaluated _needs_tick for every textile (~54 per generated house) on every 30 s substep, although with no heater on a textile can need a tick only if its own record says so
fixed.how: dry.py: _needs_tick split into _record_ticks (record-level half) + the rain and heat halves; a static index textiles_laundry.ticking (_may_tick, fields declared in TICKING_READS, built at episode start by claim_textile_moisture) holds the textiles whose record asked for a tick when the step began; the transient note _WRITTEN (World, touch-log reset token, cursor; own consumer 'textiles_laundry.fabric.written') holds the textiles written since the step began, refreshed from the touch log at the run start, inside the run after any write (a tick may write a textile later in the order) and at the run end, and moved on by the idle probe when it skips a substep (it has then seen no textile written; it also advances the consumer so the touch log can still be trimmed). With no heater active and no rain the run passes by every textile in neither set; when the step's touch log is no longer complete from its start (trimmed, then rolled back to a savepoint: len(ids) != end) or a heater is on or it rains, it scans every textile as before. Never state.
